issues.detail: The Hebrew 'הַלְאֵ֥ל יִסְכָּן גָּ֑בֶר' means 'Can a man be profitable to God?' (i.e., 'Does a man benefit God?'), not 'Can a man be inhabited by God?' The verb 'יִסְכָּן' (from סכן) means 'to profit/benefit' or 'to be useful', not 'to dwell/inhabit'. The Chinese '為神所居住' (be inhabited by God) changes the meaning entirely. The second clause 'כִּֽי יִסְכֹּ֖ן עָלֵ֣ימוֹ מַשְׂכִּֽיל' means 'for a wise man benefits himself' (i.e., a wise man profits himself), not 'He will surely care for them' (祂必眷顧他們). The subject 'מַשְׂכִּיל' (wise man) is rendered as '祂' (He) referring to God, and 'עָלֵימוֹ' (upon himself/for himself) is mistranslated as 'them' (他們). This reverses the subject and object and changes the verse's claim.
